title: End-of-day bench cleanup
summary: The 5-minute checklist that keeps the lab usable for everyone tomorrow.
hazardsMd: Standard wet-bench cleanup. Watch for sharps in unexpected places.
contentUndergrad:
## Why a checklist
Running out of pipette tips at 11pm because nobody refilled the box is a small thing that compounds across a lab. Treat the cleanup as part of the experiment.

steps.title: Survey the bench
steps.instructionMd: Look across your work area. Anything that doesn't belong on a clean bench: unboxed reagents, used tip boxes, gloves, paper. Note what needs to leave.
steps.verificationMd: You can name everything that's out of place.

steps.title: Decontaminate spills + spray surfaces
steps.instructionMd: Wipe any visible drip with paper towel + 70% ethanol. Spray the bench top, the rack of pipettes, and any shared instrument controls.
steps.safetyNotesMd: Identify spills as biohazard / chemical / unknown. Use the right cleanup for each — ethanol is not a universal solvent.
steps.verificationMd: Bench surface visibly damp from ethanol; dry within 1 min.

steps.title: Restock consumables you used
steps.instructionMd: Refill pipette tip boxes you emptied. Replace the empty waste-bag liner. Re-stock loose items in their drawer.
steps.verificationMd: Tip boxes full and lid closed. Waste container fresh-lined and within 80% capacity.

steps.title: Return shared equipment to its home
steps.instructionMd: Pipettes back in the stand. Microcentrifuge lid open. Vortex powered off. Plate reader logged out. Any reagent borrowed from a shared shelf returned to the right cabinet.
steps.verificationMd: Shared instruments visibly in their home positions. Logbooks signed for any communal-use equipment.

steps.title: Walk-around check
steps.instructionMd: Fume hood sash at the working line. Bunsen burner gas valve closed. Sharps container lid intact. Door to the lab unlocked or locked per site policy.
steps.verificationMd: All gas valves closed. Lab is in the same shape (or better) than you found it.
